name: Wukong
notes: The fight opens with Cyclone (R) at t=0 rather than at the end of the rotation: each of its 16 ticks shaves 0.5s off Crushing Blow's cooldown, and casting it first lets that cooldown reduction benefit the whole fight instead of only the tail end.

Cyclone's first 2-second spin (8 ticks every 0.25s) is always recast at the earliest opportunity, the 1s post-spin lockout, for a second 2-second spin (8 more ticks), since the dummy never fights back and the recast is strictly beneficial; the 8s recast window is never at risk. A further recast never becomes available inside a 15s fight given the 90-130s base cooldown.
Wukong keeps auto-attacking through Cyclone: only casting Q/W/E interrupts the spin, and Cyclone itself has no cast time, so the two run in parallel.
Crushing Blow (Q) has no cast time per the wiki description ('cast time = none'); the numbers sheet's castTime:0.5 for Q is treated as stale tooltip data and ignored.

Crushing Blow arms Wukong's next basic attack rather than dealing damage itself; its bonus damage and 3s armor shred land when that attack connects, Q's cooldown then starts (post-effect) and Wukong's attack timer resets for an immediate follow-up attack, exactly as described.
Crushing Blow's bonus damage is treated as non-crit, matching the wiki's note that the bonus portion is tagged as proc damage rather than basic-attack damage.

Every landed instance of Wukong's damage (plain attacks, Crushing Blow's bonus, Nimbus Strike, each Cyclone tick) shaves 0.5s off Crushing Blow's cooldown, per its own description; the empowerment window itself (5s per the wiki prose, vs a 6s BuffDuration in the bin) is never at risk of expiring unused given how often Wukong attacks, so it is not separately timed.

Nimbus Strike is cast on cooldown for its magic damage and its own 5s bonus attack speed; its two additional clone-strike targets are skipped since no other enemies exist near the dummy for them to hit.
Crushing Blow's bonus attack range is not modeled: it changes reach, not damage, and every attack in this fight lands regardless of range.

Warrior Trickster (W) is never cast: its clone is an independent auto-attacker that also mirrors Q/E/R at a reduced (40-60%) damage modifier, which would need a second attack timeline the engine does not provide. That real damage is out of scope here, so Wukong's numbers below understate his true fight damage; this is flagged rather than approximated.
Stone Skin (passive) only grants bonus armor and health regeneration, neither of which affects Wukong's outgoing damage, so it is not modeled.
Mana is not modeled: none of the costs (20/60-40/30-50/100) bind inside a 15s fight at level 16.

The engine's armor-shred field only accepts a single percentage regardless of ability rank, so the maxed rank-5 value (30%) is used at every rank tested; this understates the shred at lower ranks, which the champion rarely reaches by the levels this simulator uses (6, 11, 16).

assumed.why: the engine's shred slot reads one flat percentage, not a by-rank list, so the maxed rank-5 value is used for every fight regardless of Q's actual rank
